finding: Authoritative material does not support one singular "main gate". The university calls Krentzman one of its primary gateways, and the heaviest real arrival is Ruggles. This is case C: an urban-campus arrival space rather than a conventional gate.

candidates.name: Krentzman Quadrangle / 360 Huntington Avenue
candidates.identity: The ceremonial front door. Original campus nucleus from the 1934 invitational competition; Ell, Richards and Dodge halls front onto it; the brick ledge carrying the university seal is the graduation photo spot. 360 Huntington Avenue is the university's published address.
candidates.against: A quadrangle, not a forecourt — the space opens off the pavement, so a vehicle cannot stand in it without inventing a driveway.

candidates.name: Ruggles station / Forsyth Street
candidates.identity: The busiest real arrival: Orange Line, commuter rail and a nine-berth busway. The MBTA's own entrance here is named "Northeastern, Forsyth St".
candidates.against: Reads as a transit interchange rather than as a university; the station structure and its rail cut are heavy modelling before the district looks like anything.

candidates.name: Centennial Common
candidates.identity: The largest enclosed green inside the campus and its ceremonial heart.
candidates.against: Interior. No street frontage at all, so neither a car nor a credible first camera shot belongs here.

candidates.name: ISEC / Columbus Avenue
candidates.identity: The newest identity of the university — the science complex and the pedestrian crossing over the rail corridor.
candidates.against: Across the tracks from the historic campus; recognisable to people who know the place now, not to a general audience.
